status.label: Editor sizing needs reproduction
status.detail: Unassigned open regression; restart recovery and a later ultrawide duplicate suggest a display-dependent sizing problem, not established ownership.

next_action.label: Request editor display transition
next_action.reason: Identify the monitor/scaling transition before approving a sizing correction.

comment.body:
Thanks for the before/after screenshots and for confirming that you did not resize the editor. The 0.80.1 follow-up says restarting PowerToys restores the size, and #35262 adds an ultrawide case. These establish the symptom but not which display transition changes the size.

Please provide:
1. On the latest stable PowerToys, whether repeated open/pick/close cycles still enlarge the editor; include the tested version and whether this starts after moving between displays, sleep, docking, or a scaling change.
2. For the displays involved, the resolution and scaling shown in Windows Settings > System > Display, which is primary, and which display contains the editor before and after it grows.

This will distinguish stale per-monitor sizing from a fixed editor-layout regression. Please omit personal content from any display screenshot.

actions.label: Approve editor sizing investigation
actions.note: Lightweight candidate plan; reproduce the display transition before implementation. No fork mirror or completed design is claimed.

judgment.rationale: The editor grows without user resizing and restart can recover it. The relevant display/scaling transition is missing; no assignee or linked fixing PR was found.
evidence: The report supplies 0.79.0 screenshots and the author explicitly denies resizing: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31883#issuecomment-1996056558
The ultrawide report #35262 was closed as a duplicate of this issue, not as a fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the specific display transition and validate the candidate sizing plan against it.

fix_assessment.rationale: A module sizing correction is plausible, but the failure mechanism is unconfirmed. The reviewed timeline and issue-number PR search did not identify an existing fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep editor dimensions stable across activation and monitor changes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: editor reuse retains a stale display scale or work-area-derived size, so a later activation enlarges the fixed-size editor. Restart recovery supports retained state, but does not prove DPI is responsible.
plan: Reproduce the reported activation/display transition on the current editor and compare window pixel bounds with its logical dimensions; also reproduce on the historical 0.79/0.80 UI if necessary.

Trace editor creation, reuse and monitor sizing under src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI; change only the boundary that converts logical editor dimensions to the target display size, avoiding repeated scaling or full-work-area sizing.
Add repeated-activation and monitor-scale-change regression coverage, including ultrawide work areas and close/reopen without restarting PowerToys.
verification: On two displays with differing scaling, invoke, pick, close and reopen repeatedly before and after moving displays; the content fits and dimensions do not compound.
Repeat on an ultrawide display and after restarting PowerToys; compare against the supplied screenshots.

confidence.rationale: Retained sizing state is plausible, but no display transition or current-build reproduction establishes the mechanism.

issue_context.summary: Color Picker's non-resizable editor becomes roughly three times larger after initial use, leaving unused space. Another user reports that a restart restores it.
known_information: Reported on 0.79.0, with confirmation on 0.80.1; the author opens the editor by hotkey and does not manually resize it.
Live issue is open, labeled Issue-Bug and Severity-Regression, with no assignee.
inferences: Restart recovery suggests state retained across activations; a DPI/work-area interaction is a candidate, not a confirmed cause.
The ultrawide duplicate broadens the affected topology but does not establish that every case has the same cause.
issue_context.analysis: The existing artifact's empty-assignee ownership claim was unsupported. Preserve this issue as the canonical open report, gather the missing display discriminator, and avoid claiming a fixed or implementation-ready design.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all three comments, and enumerated the public timeline.
Read #35262, including the explicit /dup #31883 decision; no fixing PR appeared in the reviewed timeline or direct issue-number PR search.
Checked public Color Picker source ownership under src/modules/colorPicker/ColorPickerUI; the report predates substantial UI evolution, so current reproduction must precede a historical sizing patch.

information_gaps.information: Whether the enlargement still occurs on the latest stable version and which activation/display transition precedes it.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates an obsolete UI regression from retained activation state in the current editor.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Report the tested version and repeat open/pick/close cycles, noting sleep, docking, display movement or scaling changes.

information_gaps.information: Resolution, scaling, primary display and before/after editor display.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Read Windows Settings > System > Display for only the involved monitors; redact personal content from screenshots.
